title: Is this year shorter than normal 2021
paragraphs: ‘Time waits for no man’ – or so the saying goes. We can’t stop time and we can’t control it, although sometimes, in our minds, we think time flies – for example, when the weekend arrives, we feel it’s over in no time! But if this year in particular feels like it’s passing more quickly than others have done, there could be a scientific explanation why.

Of course, we know a year is usually 365 days long. Clever scientists calculated this a long time ago. They also worked out that every four years, we need an extra day to keep our calendar in sync – this is called a leap year. But 2021 isn’t one of those years, and yet it’s not behaving like a normal year. Scientists and astrophysicists have done the math and discovered the Earth is moving faster than it ever has in the last 50 years. This means that 2021 is going to be the shortest year in decades.

Apparently, this is because the Earth is spinning faster on its axis, quicker than it has done in decades, and the days are therefore shorter. But they are only short by a tiny amount – around 0.05 milliseconds – so don’t panic if you haven’t noticed! However, long-term these milliseconds add up. Astrophysicist Graham Jones and Konstantin Bikos from Time and Date told The Independent newspaper: “If the Earth’s rotation continues to quicken, we may at some point require a negative leap second. If this happens, our clocks would skip a second in order to keep up with the hurrying Earth.” Since 1972, 27 leap seconds have only been added to our time and none have been taken away.

This really is only of concern for atomic clocks – the most accurate timekeeping devices in history. Studying the Earth’s rotation and then subtracting or adding a leap second to these clocks can ensure they remain aligned and keep us on time. But now, maybe we need to get a move on before this ‘shorter’ year is gone in a split second!

vocabulary.entry: time flies 时光飞逝
vocabulary.example: How time flies! It's already the end of the year.
vocabulary.translation: 时光飞逝！转眼又到了年末。

vocabulary.term: in no time 立刻；很快
vocabulary.entry: in no time 立刻；很快
vocabulary.example: He finished the task in no time.
vocabulary.translation: 他很快就完成了任务。

vocabulary.entry: calculate /ˈkælkjuleɪt/ v. 计算；推算
vocabulary.example: The computer can calculate the result in seconds.
vocabulary.translation: 电脑能在几秒钟内算出结果。

vocabulary.term: work out 计算出；弄明白
vocabulary.entry: work out 计算出；弄明白
vocabulary.example: It took her hours to work out the math problem.
vocabulary.translation: 她花了好几个小时才解出这道数学题。

vocabulary.entry: extra /ˈekstrə/ adj. 额外的；附加的
vocabulary.example: We need extra chairs for the meeting.
vocabulary.translation: 我们需要为会议准备额外的椅子。

vocabulary.term: in sync 同步；协调一致
vocabulary.entry: in sync 同步；协调一致
vocabulary.example: The sound and picture must be in sync.
vocabulary.translation: 声音和画面必须保持同步。

vocabulary.entry: leap year /liːp jɪə/ n. 闰年
vocabulary.example: 2024 is a leap year with 366 days.
vocabulary.translation: 2024年是闰年，有366天。

vocabulary.entry: astrophysicist /ˌæstrəʊˈfɪzɪsɪst/ n. 天体物理学家
vocabulary.example: The astrophysicist studies the origin of the universe.
vocabulary.translation: 这位天体物理学家研究宇宙的起源。

vocabulary.term: do the math 计算；算账
vocabulary.entry: do the math 计算；算账
vocabulary.example: Do the math and you'll see we can't afford it.
vocabulary.translation: 算一算你就知道我们买不起。

vocabulary.entry: decade /ˈdekeɪd/ n. 十年
vocabulary.example: Great changes have taken place in the past decade.
vocabulary.translation: 过去十年间发生了巨大的变化。

vocabulary.entry: spin /spɪn/ v. （使）旋转
vocabulary.example: The Earth spins on its axis once every 24 hours.
vocabulary.translation: 地球每24小时绕地轴自转一周。

vocabulary.entry: axis /ˈæksɪs/ n. 轴；地轴
vocabulary.example: The Earth rotates around its axis.
vocabulary.translation: 地球绕着地轴自转。

vocabulary.entry: tiny /ˈtaɪni/ adj. 极小的；微小的
vocabulary.example: A tiny insect landed on her hand.
vocabulary.translation: 一只小虫子落在了她的手上。

vocabulary.entry: millisecond /ˈmɪlisekənd/ n. 毫秒
vocabulary.example: The reaction time is measured in milliseconds.
vocabulary.translation: 反应时间以毫秒为单位计算。

vocabulary.entry: add up 累积；合计
vocabulary.example: These small expenses add up over time.
vocabulary.translation: 这些小额开支日积月累会变得不少。

vocabulary.entry: rotation /rəʊˈteɪʃn/ n. 旋转；自转
vocabulary.example: The rotation of the Earth causes day and night.
vocabulary.translation: 地球的自转形成了昼夜交替。

vocabulary.entry: quicken /ˈkwɪkən/ v. 加快；加速
vocabulary.example: The pace of life quickens in big cities.
vocabulary.translation: 大城市的生活节奏更快。

vocabulary.entry: negative leap second /ˈneɡətɪv liːp ˈsekənd/ n. 负闰秒
vocabulary.example: A negative leap second may be needed if Earth spins faster.
vocabulary.translation: 如果地球自转加快，或许就需要引入负闰秒。

vocabulary.entry: skip /skɪp/ v. 跳过；略过
vocabulary.example: You can skip the boring parts of the book.
vocabulary.translation: 你可以跳过这本书里无聊的部分。

vocabulary.entry: hurrying /ˈhʌriɪŋ/ adj. 疾驰的；快速移动的
vocabulary.example: We chased the hurrying train but failed to catch it.
vocabulary.translation: 我们追赶疾驰的火车，但没赶上。

vocabulary.entry: atomic clock /əˈtɒmɪk klɒk/ n. 原子钟
vocabulary.example: Atomic clocks are used for precise timekeeping.
vocabulary.translation: 原子钟被用于精准计时。

vocabulary.entry: accurate /ˈækjərət/ adj. 精确的；准确的
vocabulary.example: The watch is accurate to within a second a day.
vocabulary.translation: 这块手表一天的误差不超过一秒。

vocabulary.entry: timekeeping device /ˈtaɪmkiːpɪŋ dɪˈvaɪs/ n. 计时工具
vocabulary.example: A sundial was an ancient timekeeping device.
vocabulary.translation: 日晷是一种古老的计时工具。

vocabulary.entry: subtract /səbˈtrækt/ v. 减去；扣除
vocabulary.example: Subtract 5 from 10 and you get 5.

vocabulary.entry: split second /splɪt ˈsekənd/ n. 一瞬间；一刹那
vocabulary.example: The car passed by in a split second.
vocabulary.translation: 那辆车一瞬间就开过去了。

sentences.english: ‘Time waits for no man’ – or so the saying goes.
We can’t stop time and we can’t control it, although sometimes, in our minds, we think time flies – for example, when the weekend arrives, we feel it’s over in no time!
sentences.chinese: 我们既无法让时间停下脚步，也不能掌控它的流逝，不过有时候在我们的感觉里，时间过得飞快——比如周末明明刚到，转眼就结束了！

sentences.english: But if this year in particular feels like it’s passing more quickly than others have done, there could be a scientific explanation why.
sentences.chinese: 但如果你觉得今年的时光流逝得格外快，这背后或许有科学的解释。

sentences.english: Of course, we know a year is usually 365 days long.
sentences.chinese: 我们当然都知道，一年通常有365天。

sentences.english: Clever scientists calculated this a long time ago.
sentences.chinese: 很久以前，聪慧的科学家们就算出了这个结果。

sentences.english: They also worked out that every four years, we need an extra day to keep our calendar in sync – this is called a leap year.
sentences.chinese: 他们还发现，每四年我们需要额外增加一天，才能让日历与地球公转周期保持同步——这一年被称为闰年。

sentences.english: But 2021 isn’t one of those years, and yet it’s not behaving like a normal year.
sentences.chinese: 但2021年不是闰年，然而它异于往常。

sentences.english: Scientists and astrophysicists have done the math and discovered the Earth is moving faster than it ever has in the last 50 years.
sentences.chinese: 科学家和天体物理学家经过计算发现，地球的自转速度达到了过去50年来的最快水平。

sentences.english: This means that 2021 is going to be the shortest year in decades.
sentences.chinese: 这意味着2021年将成为几十年来最短的一年。

sentences.english: Apparently, this is because the Earth is spinning faster on its axis, quicker than it has done in decades, and the days are therefore shorter.
sentences.chinese: 显然，这是因为地球绕地轴的自转速度创下了数十年以来的新高，所以每一天的时长都变短了。

sentences.english: But they are only short by a tiny amount – around 0.05 milliseconds – so don’t panic if you haven’t noticed!
sentences.chinese: 不过这种缩短的幅度极小，大约只有0.05毫秒，所以就算你毫无察觉也不必惊慌！

sentences.english: However, long-term these milliseconds add up.
sentences.chinese: 但从长远来看，这些毫秒的差距会不断累积。

sentences.english: Astrophysicist Graham Jones and Konstantin Bikos from Time and Date told The Independent newspaper: “If the Earth’s rotation continues to quicken, we may at some point require a negative leap second.
sentences.chinese: 时间与日期网站的天体物理学家格雷厄姆·琼斯和康斯坦丁·比科斯在接受《独立报》采访时表示：“如果地球自转速度持续加快，未来某一天我们或许需要引入负闰秒。

sentences.english: If this happens, our clocks would skip a second in order to keep up with the hurrying Earth.”
sentences.chinese: 一旦实施负闰秒，为了跟上地球的自转节奏，我们的时钟就要跳过一秒钟。”

sentences.english: Since 1972, 27 leap seconds have only been added to our time and none have been taken away.
sentences.chinese: 自1972年以来，人类只给时间增加过27次闰秒，从未减少过一秒。

sentences.english: This really is only of concern for atomic clocks – the most accurate timekeeping devices in history.
sentences.chinese: 这件事其实只关乎原子钟——这种有史以来最精准的计时工具。

sentences.english: Studying the Earth’s rotation and then subtracting or adding a leap second to these clocks can ensure they remain aligned and keep us on time.
sentences.chinese: 通过监测地球自转，并相应地给原子钟增减闰秒，就能确保它们与地球自转保持同步，让我们的时间始终准确无误。

sentences.english: But now, maybe we need to get a move on before this ‘shorter’ year is gone in a split second!
sentences.chinese: 不过话说回来，或许我们得抓紧时间行动起来，免得这“更短”的一年一眨眼就过去了！
